'''Assyr Abdulle''' (19 January 1971 – 1 September 2021) was a Swiss mathematician.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/assyr-abdulle-1971-2021-3/|title=Assyr Abdulle, 1971-2021.|journal=EPFL|date=9 March 2021|language=French}}</ref> He specialized in numerical mathematics.

==Biography==
Abdulle earned a doctorate in mathematics under [[Gerhard Wanner]] and [[Ernst Hairer]] at the [[University of Geneva]] with the thesis ''Méthodes de Chebyshev basées sur des polynômes orthogonaux''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=112132|title=Assyr Abdulle|work=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> He also earned a degree in violin and music from the [[Conservatoire de Musique de Genève]] in 1993. From 2001 to 2002, he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at [[Princeton University]] and worked at the computational laboratory at [[ETH Zurich]] from 2002 to 2003. In 2003, he became an assistant professor at the [[University of Basel]] and an associate professor at the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 2007. He then became a full professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/anmc/|title=Welcome to the Chair of Computational Mathematics and Numerical Analysis held by Prof. Assyr Abdulle|work=EPFL}}</ref> At the school, he started the master's degree in [[computational science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/anmc/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Flash_article_CSE_2016.pdf|title=Model of knowledge: EPFL's Master in Computational Science & Engineering|date=9 March 2016|work=EPFL|language=French}}</ref> In 2016, he became Director of the Institut Mathicse and was founding Director of the Institut de Mathématiques in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.epfl.ch/schools/sb/research/math/|title=Institute of Mathematics – MATH|work=EPFL}}</ref>

Abdulle was impassioned with modeling and numerical simulations in biology, chemistry, geology, and medicine.<ref>{{cite news |last=Abdulle|first=Assyr|date=2009|title=The finite element heterogeneous multiscale method: a computational strategy for multiscale PDEs|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=Gakkōtosho|location=Tokyo|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Henning|first2=Patrick|date=2017|title=Multiscale methods for wave problems in heterogeneous media|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=Elsevier/North-Holland|location=Amsterdam|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=E|first2=Weinan|last3=Engquist|first3=Björn|last4=Vanden-Eijnden|first4=Eric|date=2012|title=The heterogeneous multiscale method|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=University Press|location=Cambridge|access-date=}}</ref> He notably contributed to the development of heterogeneous multi-scale methods. He developed methods for solving multiscale and ergodic stochastic problems.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Vilmart|first2=Gilles|last3=Zygalakis|first3=Konstantinos|date=2014|title=High order numerical approximation of the invariant measure of ergodic SDEs|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=SIAM|location= |access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Pavliotis|first2=Grigorios A.|last3=Vaes|first3=Urbain|date=2017|title=Spectral methods for multiscale stochastic differential equations|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=SIAM|location= |access-date=}}</ref> He also invented the Orthogonal Runge-Kutta-Chebyshev,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Medovikov|first2=Alexei A.|date=2002|title=Second order Chebyshev methods based on orthogonal polynomials|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=Springer|location= |access-date=}}</ref> which was used to solve stiff differential equations which were then generalized to multiscale stochastic systems.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Cirille|first2=Stephane|date=2008|title=Chebyshev methods for stiff stochastic differential equations|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=SIAM|location= |access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abdulle|first1=Assyr|last2=Almuslimani |first2=Ibrahim|last3=Vilmart|first3=Gilles|date=2018|title=Optimal explicit stabilized integrator of weak order 1 for stiff and ergodic stochastic differential equations|trans-title= |url= |language= |work=SIAM|location= |access-date=}}</ref>

In 2005, Abdulle won the New Talent Award at the International Conference on Scientific Computation and Differential Equations.<ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date=18 April 2005|title=Scicade New Talent-Preis an Prof. Dr. Assyr Abdulle|trans-title= |url=https://www.unibas.ch/de/Aktuell/News/Ehrungen-und-Mitgliedschaften/Scicade-New-Talent-Preis-an-Prof.-Dr.-Assyr-Abdulle.html|language=German|work=[[University of Basel]]|location= |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref> He received an advanced research fellowship from the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/projects/advanced-research-fellowship-multiscale-methods-for-nonlinear-pro|title=Advanced Research Fellowship: Multiscale methods for nonlinear problems in strongly heterogenous media and stiff stochastic systems|work=The University of Edinburgh}}</ref> In 2009, he won the [[James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://evoq-eval.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/james-h-wilkinson-prize-in-numerical-analysis-and-scientific-computing#Prize-History|title=Prize History|work=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200909/rtx090901119p.pdf|title=Mathematics People|date=October 2009|work=AMS}}</ref> awarded by the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], for his contributions to applied mathematics.<ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date=30 June 2009|title=Professor honored with prestigious award for work in computational mathematics|trans-title= |url=https://archive.siam.org/about/news-siam.php?id=1581|language= |work=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|location= |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref> He won the Germund Dahlquist Prize in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/germund-dahlquist-prize#Prize-History|title=Prize History|work=SIAM}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/SIAMDahlquist/|title=SIAM Germund Dahlquist Prize|work=Maths History}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Paz Calvo|first=Mari|date=1 May 2014|title=Assyr Abdulle Receives 2013 SIAM Dahlquist Prize|trans-title= |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/assyr-abdulle-receives-2013-siam-dahlquist-prize|language= |work=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|location= |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

Assyr Abdulle died on 1 September 2021 at the age of 50.<ref name=obit/>
